title: What If Russia Fired One Nuke at Japan's Fleet?
description:
What would happen if Russia fired one nuclear weapon at Japanese and American warships off Hokkaido?

In this simulation, a nuclear Kalibr cruise missile gives the fleet 27 minutes of warning, then bursts as a 10-kiloton air burst over open sea after a week-long crisis over the Kuril Islands.

Eleven thirty-seven, off Hokkaido: the first nuclear weapon used in war since Nagasaki. Twenty-seven minutes earlier, a Russian submarine in the Sea of Okhotsk fired a cruise missile at the fleet. Why would Russia fire at ships and not a city, and what do Tokyo and Washington do with the half hour they have? Before the simulation we look at what is real: islands four kilometres from Japan, the Bastion missile batteries Russia put on them, and the peace treaty that was never signed.

This is a simulation. It has not happened. The collision, the escalation, the nuclear step, the yield and the wind are fictional design choices built from published models and open sources, not predictions of any government's policy, and tied to no real date.
